title: Cross-sectional ranking objective for the crypto ENTRY model: rank the perps against each other at each decision time instead of predicting each one's R alone

frontier.baseline: the same recipe on the raw per-asset net-R regression target, same 13 monthly origins, graded on actual net R of outright trades at the canonical cost stack
frontier.consumer: src/units/strategies/ml_entry.py (D3) on bybit_2 real money + mirror + prop
frontier.est_cost: $0 runner (~2 h); needs a lambdarank arm in the ml_entry_residual harness
frontier.next_step: unit RQ-20261112-4654-06 (RULE-RQ20261112-4654-06-XSDEMEAN-TARGET, decide_vs_raw: paired >= +0.06, CI low > 0, n >= 300 over 13 windows; baseline RAW net of full cost stack) rides PR #25559 with the harness arm; grade when it lands. Top-k-per-timestamp policy arm is the PASS follow-up.
frontier.source: arXiv 2512.08124 (long-only crypto portfolio by ranking assets, NN; title+summary, PRIMARY abstract) and 2606.27670 CryptoGAT (cross-asset graph beats per-asset temporal models; summary only); same mechanism as RESID-ENTRY (98e3-23 SIDE-DRIVER: the model prices the common factor)
frontier.why: a ranking objective is market-neutral by construction (only relative order at a timestamp matters), so it is the strong form of the residual-target idea; it also uses the whole 48-60 perp cross-section, which is the breadth lever the 2026-11-12 audit names for making Foxhound-1's edge verifiable
